STANDING ORDERS

Rule 14

This station shall be kept by TWO keepers at all hours. The machinery cannot be worked single-handed in weather.

Saltmere Board of Lights
1874 (amended 1919)
To the keepers of Kettle Rock

The Lucy Gale and her forty souls thank you for the night of 14th September.

Capt. R. Hale

3 Aug 1942
Tank drained overnight. No leak. Oily hand marks on the cap. Small hand.
— W.B.

19 Aug
Again. Taught the boy the engine. Told him: never come down here alone after dark. He laughed.

Walter says it's two of us because of the engine. That's not why, is it? He won't go below after dark without me. Nor me without him. I'm not scared. I'm only asking.

— Tom

SALTMERE BOARD OF LIGHTS · RELIEF DUTY · 1942

Autumn, 1942. American supply ships depend on Kettle Rock Light to reach Saltmere through the Atlantic storms. One week ago, both keepers vanished; no one knows what happened to them. You are the replacement crew: keep the passage open, and find out what they left behind. Their last watch is still written in the logbook.
You are in the House. Read at your own pace; the watch waits for both keepers.

FLOOR 2 · RESTORE POWER Fuel the generator. Feed the circuits. FLOOR 1 · STOP THE FLOOD Repair the pipe. Keep the pump running. FLOOR 4 · RADIO AND BEACON Send the report. Guide ships with the beam. FLOOR 3 · YOUR BEDROOM Rest here together when the watch is done.
Share clues with your partner. Both keepers can use every tool.

LEFT STICK — walk. Hold A to run. RIGHT STICK — turn. GRIP — hold tools and controls; release to let go. TRIGGER — select menus; use a held tool. B — recall your objective and last message. HOLD B — keep them visible. X — hold your breath. Y or WRIST GLANCE — recall guidance. LEFT MENU BUTTON — settings and Owen’s orders.
Contains jump scares and possession. Skip or finish to begin; reopen from the left Menu button.

Five nights of teamwork and survival horror. Contains scares.
Endless watches. All stations, no horror. Only the flood ends your run.

American supply ships need this passage. You and your partner keep the lighthouse working through the storm. Repair the machinery, clear each convoy by radio, then guide it past the rocks. Each new watch brings faster flooding and tighter aiming. Day 1 is practice: learn every job without a flood loss. From Day 2, rising water can end your watch.
No horror. No night limit. Flooding is the only loss.
